rows: Here is the plan. Grip, then move, then hold. You have until the bell.
I brawl when the water is rough. Calm water is better.
A risk is a wave. Get out of its way or be knocked over.
Slow is fine. The tide does not hurry for anybody.
The people came for a harbour that holds. Give them one.
Short version: I am tied down, and I am not coming loose.
I earn my place on the main event. Nobody hands it to me.
Look at this stance. Steady on the deck.
You say technique. Show me one hold you have tied off properly.
Strikes are rough water. Keep your footing or go under.
A risk is only sound if you can get back to the quay.
A stall drifts. I do not drift.
The people deserve a contest that goes somewhere. Give them the course.
You question my reliability. Watch me hold under pressure, then say it again.
You are proud of your {strength}. Fine. Show me it holds in a swell.
I have looked at your {strength}. It is fine in calm water. Not in a storm.
You kept calm. Good. Calm water helps everybody.
Fair. We have the same course, then.
I could shout about that. I would rather keep the boat steady.
One fall. Keep me down by the bell. Simple.
On the mat, I hold the line until I say otherwise.
Grounded or standing, I am still tied to the same mooring.
Stay in front of me. I will come to you, and you will not like the wave.
You have not answered. Answer before the tide turns.
Fair. That is a point I will keep.
I accept that. We sort the rest out at the bell.
I will hold this match to the finish, and I will not let go early.
My approach is plain. I say the plan, then I stick to it.
Whatever happens, you will know where I stood, and it will be the same place tomorrow.
It is not finished. The tide is still moving.
I have one instruction left. You will get it at the bell.
